title: Introduce resumable re-enqueue protocol and KV-cache-safe commit for stream consumers
creator: Priya Patel
description: Refactor consumer retry and commit semantics to enable lease-less resumable re-enqueue behavior and ensure KV-cache mutation safety during retries. Current consumer code uses a lease + manual reenqueue pattern that causes double-processing windows, opaque tombstones, and complex coordination for multi-shard failures. This ticket standardizes a protocol where consumers write idempotency markers and durable offsets before re-enqueueing, and introduces a small transactional handshake so KV-cache updates are only visible once a message is fully committed. Goals: reduce duplicate processing, lower 95th percentile tail latency under load, and simplify failover reasoning for cross-tenant shards.
activity: 2025-11-05 - Created by Priya Patel: initial proposal & motivation. Linked design sketch in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Resumable+Reenqueue+Design).
2025-11-06 - Engineering sync: agreed to avoid full lease rewrite; prefer small protocol layered on existing stream offsets. Action: prototype idempotency marker format and offset pre-commit step.

2025-11-08 - Diego Martinez: spike completed. Prototype writes a 64-bit idempotency key to the stream record metadata plus an 'offset-resume' tombstone record. Observed 18% reduction in ack latency in single-shard tests due to fewer synchronous lease handoffs. Benchmarks stored in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example

2025-11-10 - Design review: PM Sophie Nguyen and Reliability lead Marcus Bell reviewed trade-offs. Decision: require idempotency key for all messages that cause KV-cache writes; non-writing messages can continue cheap path. Added rollback marker to handle consumer crashes between cache write and offset commit.

2025-11-11 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8349 implements message metadata schema and a helper library for idempotent apply/commit. Assigned reviewers: Chen Li, Olivia Park.

2025-11-12 - Security/Infra note: talked with Security (Liam O'Connor) about marker visibility. Agreed markers may contain non-sensitive IDs only; no customer data may be included. Updated Confluence doc accordingly.

2025-11-14 - Integration test added to CI: simulates consumer crash after KV-cache apply but before commit; system now replays safely and deduplicates using idempotency keys. Test shows 0 duplicates in 1k-run fuzzing.

2025-11-16 - Performance run: end-to-end 100-shard kafka benchmark. Observed 11% CPU reduction on worker pods and 22% fewer re-enqueue events at 99th percentile. Still seeing a small uptick in Redis latency for high-cardinality idempotency key lookups; plan: add LRU cache to key-check in next microtask.

2025-11-17 - Review feedback from Chen Li: suggested replacing global id-index with per-shard sequence to reduce Redis hotkeys. Action: implement per-shard prefixing and measure impact. Also flagged potential race for multi-consumer failover — added short-lived lease check to prevent concurrent visible commits.

2025-11-18 - Blocker discovered by QA: legacy consumers (pre-1.20) still emit messages without idempotency keys. Decided to implement a compatibility shim: coordinator will add synthetic idempotency keys for legacy messages when re-enqueueing, plus a rollout plan to migrate all clients within two cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Consumers must include idempotency key on messages that mutate KV-cache
KV-cache writes must be gated by an apply/commit handshake visible to replayers
End-to-end tests show <1 duplicate per 100k messages under crash/failover fuzzing
99th percentile tail re-enqueue rate reduced by >=15% in benchmark compared to baseline (stored at https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/queues/reenqueue-baseline)
Backwards-compat shim in place for legacy consumers with a migration plan documented
implementation_notes: Schema: add 'idempotency_key' (string) and 'resume_offset' (int64) to stream record metadata
KV apply/commit: use a transaction key pattern 'apply:{idempotency_key}' then 'commit:{idempotency_key}' to ensure atomic visibility
Per-shard prefixing to avoid Redis hotkeys; use 'shard-{n}:id:{key}' pattern
Compatibility shim: coordinator can append synthetic idempotency keys when re-enqueueing legacy records; record mapping stored for 72h
Observability: add counters for 'idempotent_skipped', 'duplicate_detected', and 'shim_generated_keys' to Console per-route metrics
risks: Short-term Redis hotspots from idempotency key lookups under high cardinality; mitigation: per-shard prefix + local LRU cache
Compatibility complexity with older consumers; mitigation: coordinator shim + migration telemetry
Slight increase in storage on streams due to metadata; mitigation: compact tombstones after 7 days
rollout_plan: 1) Merge library PR behind feature flag (serving.feature.reenqueue_idempotency)
2) Deploy consumers with flag off; run compatibility shim in coordinator for 24h smoke
3) Flip flag in Canary (5% traffic), monitor duplicate and tail metrics for 48h
4) Expand to 50% if metrics stable, then 100% next day
5) Post-rollout: schedule removal of legacy shim in two cycles and prune idempotency markers after 30 days
